label: iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5, arm64 on Apple M5 Pro)
claim: Not a device: simulator, emulator or desktop browser on a Mac. Real-device rows are pending hardware, and no claim of meeting a device target is made from this file.

build.app: Release (-O, whole-module); UI test launches in benchmark mode

ops.note: `try bench.benchAdd(a:b:)` on the main actor: encode, `callSync` through the C ABI, decode, through the generated binding
`try bench.benchEchoBytes(data:)` with 1,024 bytes: the payload crosses the boundary twice (a byte string, which is cheaper than a record of the same size)
`bench.benchListInsert(i: 5000)` on about 10,000 rows: the call, the core's recorded insert, the one-operation patch, applied to the mirror's list before the call returns
`bench.benchTouchSignals(k: 100)`: one call, one change-set of 100 entries, applied to 100 `@Observable` properties of the mirror before the call returns

cold.note: a 100 KB snapshot is 1000 to-dos of 80 characters (the host row restores four stores of 250 rows of 100 bytes); load = `UndraCore.load` of the linked core, which starts the runtime and its core thread; the C library is statically linked, so there is no dlopen

drain.note: merged frame = the drain(s) that consumed one burst, summed: decode and apply of the merged patch to the `@Observable` store
drain.producer: a thread of its own commits the burst (the core's side of a socket or a timer): the main thread's cost of a frame is the drain at the next frame, as `DrainStats.duration` times it (`ContinuousClock`)

unmerged_estimate.method: the drain of a single entry (a call on the main thread drains before it returns, so the drain listener times a drain of exactly one change-set of one entry applied on its own), 2000 of them, median; times 1667. The runtime was not reverted: this is what applying every entry on its own would cost, from the entry cost measured here
